scenario: A traveling merchant has lost the map to the only safe road through a dangerous stretch of forest.
instruction_frame: a request to narrate a brief scene
instruction: Can you tell me a brief story about someone helping a merchant who's lost their map in a dangerous forest?
response:
The merchant stood at the forest's edge, frantically searching through his wagon. His map was gone—the only guide through miles of treacherous terrain where travelers routinely vanished.

Tom approached from the nearby village, carrying firewood. He noticed the merchant's distress and paused. "Everything alright?"

The merchant explained his predicament, voice tight with worry. He had to reach the eastern trade post by week's end, but without the map, he'd never make it through safely.

Tom set down his bundle. "I know the safe path," he said quietly. "Grew up near here. I can draw you a new map."

He borrowed parchment and carefully sketched the route, marking the reliable creek crossings and noting which clearings to avoid. He added details about landmarks—a lightning-split oak, a moss-covered boulder—so the merchant wouldn't lose his way.

"There," Tom said, handing it over. "Follow this exactly. Should take you three days."

The merchant thanked him profusely, offering payment, but Tom waved it off and picked up his firewood. "Safe travels," he said, heading back toward the village as the merchant studied his new map with relief.
